c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Jiro, a celebrated sake brewer in an Edo fishing village, watches the annual shrine festival descend into chaos when his prized barrel rolls into the sacred pond, yet discovers the accident creates the village's most harmonious celebration in decades.

g.passage: Jiro, the brewer whose cedar-aged sake had won the daimyo's praise three winters running, watched in horror as his prized barrel slipped from the festival cart and rolled down the slope toward the sacred pond ______ frozen beside the torii gate, he could do nothing but listen to the splash, the startled shouts, and then, unexpectedly, the laughter of the whole village wading in after it.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 "Jiro ... watched ..."라는 완전한 독립절이다. 빈칸 뒤 "standing frozen beside the torii gate"는 분사구이지만, 그 뒤에 "he could do nothing but listen"이라는 주절이 이어지므로 빈칸 뒤도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표 하나로 두 독립절을 이은 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이다. 처음의 긴 동격구 때문에 B가 자연스러워 보이기 쉽다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 무종지문이고, D는 등위접속사 so 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 접속사와 절을 갈라놓는다.
g.explanation_en: The part before the blank, "Jiro ... watched ...," is a complete independent clause. After the blank, the participial phrase "standing frozen beside the torii gate" leads into the main clause "he could do nothing but listen," so the text after the blank is also an independent clause. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so A is correct. B joins them with only a comma, which is a comma splice. The long appositive at the start can make B look natural. C has no punctuation at all, so it creates a run-on sentence. D adds an unnecessary comma after the conjunction "so," which separates the conjunction from the clause it introduces.
g.design: I placed a long appositive at the start and a participial phrase right after the blank. This makes the clause boundary hard to see, and you have to find the main clause later in the sentence to judge the punctuation. All four options use the same frame ("standing"), so the comma splice and the misplaced comma can only be ruled out by comparing them.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Alemayehu receives a letter from her estranged sister during the Ethiopian coffee ceremony, arriving twenty years late, rekindling hope that forgiveness might still bloom across the distance that separated them.

g.passage: Alemayehu poured the first round of coffee, the strong abol that her mother had always insisted be served to the eldest guest ______ envelope, its stamps faded and its corners softened by twenty years in a misdirected mailbag, lay unopened beside the incense burner, her sister's careful handwriting still visible through the dust.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 'Alemayehu poured the first round of coffee'라는 독립절에 긴 동격어구(the strong abol ... eldest guest)가 붙은 문장이고, 빈칸 뒤 'envelope ... lay unopened ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 마침표로 나누어야 하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표가 동격어구를 닫아 주는 것처럼 보이지만, 쉼표 하나로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 run-on 문장이 된다. D는 등위접속사 and를 쓴 점은 맞지만 and 뒤에 쉼표를 찍으면 안 되므로 틀렸다.
g.explanation_en: Before the blank, you have an independent clause, "Alemayehu poured the first round of coffee," followed by a long appositive ("the strong abol ... eldest guest"). After the blank comes another independent clause: "envelope ... lay unopened ...". Two independent clauses must be properly separated, and the period in B does exactly that. A seems to close off the appositive with a comma, but a single comma between two independent clauses makes a comma splice. C has no punctuation at all, so it creates a run-on sentence. D uses the conjunction "and" correctly, but you shouldn't put a comma after "and," so D is also wrong.
g.design: A long appositive comes right before the blank, which hides where one independent clause ends and the next begins. Choice A looks like it just closes the appositive with a comma, and choice D adds a coordinating conjunction, so both seem partly correct and have to be compared carefully against the answer.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Linh and a stranger lock eyes over steaming pho in a Hanoi dawn alley, each recognizing in the other's weathered face the ghost of a choice they made differently, then part forever.

g.passage: Across the narrow alley, a woman about Linh's age sat hunched over her own bowl of pho, her hands, cracked and stained with what looked like years of factory dye, wrapped around the chipped porcelain for ______ when she finally looked up through the steam, Linh saw in that weathered face the life she herself had refused twenty years earlier.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞은 'a woman ... sat hunched'라는 독립절이고, 그 뒤에 'her hands ... wrapped ...'라는 독립분사구(절대구)가 붙어 있다. 빈칸 뒤 'Linh saw ...' 역시 'when' 부사절이 앞에 놓인 독립절이므로, 두 독립절을 잇는 세미콜론을 쓴 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 문장부호가 없어 융합문이 되고, 'warmth when'으로 붙어 읽혀 의미도 흐려진다. D의 'then'은 접속부사이지 등위접속사가 아니므로 쉼표로는 두 절을 이을 수 없다.
g.explanation_en: The text before the blank is an independent clause ("a woman ... sat hunched"), followed by an absolute phrase ("her hands ... wrapped ..."). After the blank comes another independent clause ("Linh saw ...") that opens with a "when" clause. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, so C is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. B uses no punctuation at all, so it creates a run-on and wrongly makes "when" seem to attach to "warmth." D uses "then," which is an adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, so a comma before it still leaves a comma splice.
g.design: There is a long absolute phrase with commas inside it before the boundary, so a quick reader may miss that the main clause has already finished. The distractors use a comma, no punctuation, and comma + "then," which all look plausible.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Prospector Cornelius finds a half-starved mule wandering his Gold Rush camp and names it Duchess, only to realize the stubborn creature's refusal to work harder than necessary contains more wisdom than any fortune.

g.passage: Cornelius had expected the half-starved mule he found wandering his Gold Rush camp to repay his kindness with labor. Instead, Duchess—having eaten three days of his oats, dozed through the morning heat, and stopped cold whenever the ore cart grew heavier than she ______ watched him strain at the sluice box with what looked unmistakably like pity.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 주어 Duchess 뒤의 긴 삽입구는 대시로 시작했으므로 같은 부호인 대시로 닫아야 하고, 그래야 주어가 본동사 watched와 연결된다. 따라서 정답은 D이다. A는 삽입구를 닫는 쉼표처럼 보여 그럴듯하지만, 대시로 연 삽입구를 쉼표로 닫을 수 없다. B의 세미콜론은 주어 Duchess와 동사 watched 사이를 끊어 앞뒤 모두 완전한 절이 되지 못한다. C는 문장부호가 없어서 삽입구가 끝나는 곳이 표시되지 않고, she liked watched처럼 동사가 엉켜 읽힌다.
g.explanation_en: The long interrupting phrase after the subject "Duchess" opens with a dash, so it has to close with a dash too. That closing dash lets the subject connect to its main verb, "watched," which makes D correct. A looks reasonable because a comma could close an interruption, but you can't close a dash-opened interruption with a comma. B uses a semicolon that cuts the subject "Duchess" off from its verb "watched," so neither side is a complete clause. C has no punctuation at all, so nothing marks where the interruption ends, and "she liked watched" reads as a jumble of verbs.
g.design: This is a two-step check. First, notice that the dash opens an interruption. Second, find the main verb "watched" after the long list. Distractors A and C each offer a plausible boundary, so you have to compare them against the opening dash to rule them out.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.
- 세부 기술 힌트: 삽입구·동격·긴 수식어 뒤에서 절 경계(콜론/대시/세미콜론/쉼표+등위접속사)를 판단하거나, 필수/비필수 수식어 쉼표를 가리는 문제. 선택지는 문장부호/접속 조합 4개.
c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Giorgi, an old shepherd in a Soviet Georgian village, receives a message from his son written before the war but delivered long after, its words becoming the mountain echo he needed to finally hear.

g.passage: The letter had been written in the spring of 1941 and had wandered through three postal depots before it reached the village. Giorgi, who had not heard his son's voice in nearly thirty years, unfolded the brittle page beside the sheepfold______ a careful schoolboy hand, Levan had promised to come home when the snow left the pass, and the old man read the line aloud until the mountains seemed to answer.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Giorgi ... unfolded the brittle page beside the sheepfold"는 삽입절이 있어도 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 "in a careful schoolboy hand, Levan had promised..."도 주어 Levan과 동사 had promised를 가진 독립절이다. 독립절 두 개는 세미콜론으로 이어야 하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙인 run-on이며, "sheepfold in a careful hand"처럼 앞 절에 붙는 전치사구로 잘못 읽히게 된다. D는 which가 관계절을 만들지만 그 절 안에 Levan had promised라는 주어·동사가 따로 있어서 which가 들어갈 자리가 없으므로 문법적으로 성립하지 않는다.
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "Giorgi ... unfolded the brittle page beside the sheepfold," make a complete independent clause, even with the long "who" clause in the middle. The words after the blank, "in a careful schoolboy hand, Levan had promised...," make a second independent clause with the subject Levan and the verb had promised. You need a semicolon to join two independent clauses, so A is correct. B joins them with only a comma, which is a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on and makes the phrase look like it describes the sheepfold. D adds "which," but the clause already has its own subject and verb (Levan had promised), so "which" has no role and the sentence falls apart.
g.design: I put a long nonessential clause right after the subject so students have to find the main clause before they can see that two independent clauses meet at the blank. B and D look like they could work, because the opening prepositional phrase makes a comma seem natural.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Professor Aksel teaches his final sauna lesson to three fishermen, instructing them that the proper temperature for wisdom is the exact moment before the body rebels against comfort itself.

g.passage: Professor Aksel, who had taught in the cramped cedar sauna behind the harbor for thirty winters, ladled water onto the hissing stones and gave the three fishermen his final lesson______ the proper temperature for wisdom, he said, was the exact moment before the body rebels against comfort itself.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.explanation: 긴 비필수 관계절 뒤에서 주절은 'gave the three fishermen his final lesson'으로 끝나는 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'the proper temperature ... was ...'도 독립절이며 그 lesson의 내용을 설명한다. 따라서 앞 절의 내용을 풀어 주는 콜론을 쓴 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 세미콜론 뒤에 'that'으로 시작하는 명사절이 와서 독립절이 아닌 단편이 된다. D는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 run-on 문장이다.
g.explanation_en: After the long nonrestrictive clause, the main clause ends at "gave the three fishermen his final lesson," and it can stand on its own. The words after the blank, "the proper temperature ... was ...," make up another independent clause, and that clause explains what the lesson was. A colon is the right way to introduce an explanation like this, so B is correct. A joins two independent clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts a semicolon before a "that" noun clause, and that clause can't stand alone, so it's a fragment. D runs the two independent clauses together with no punctuation.
g.design: The long relative clause hides where the main clause ends. Students have to see that both sides of the blank are independent clauses, and then check the context to see that the second clause explains the "lesson," which is why a colon fits. Choice C looks plausible because it uses a semicolon, but the "that" clause after it can't stand alone.

c.instruction:
- medium: 표준 SAT 중간 난이도. 두 단계 판단(규칙 적용 + 문맥 확인, 또는 두 정보의 연결)이 필요하다. 정답은 정독하면 명확하지만 훑어 읽으면 틀리게 설계한다. 오답 3개 중 최소 2개는 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 비교해야만 배제되고, 나머지 하나도 말이 되어야 한다.

c.seed: an excerpt of literary fiction (novel/short story scene) — Émile borrows his neighbor's fishing net to repair his own, then watches it disappear into the bayou's mouth alongside the only friendship that ever understood his silences.

g.passage: Émile had borrowed the net from Thibodeaux, the old neighbor who never once asked him to explain the long, wordless evenings he spent on the porch______ by the time the tide turned, the net had slipped from its cypress stake and was drifting, slowly and then all at once, toward the bayou's mouth.
g.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
g.design: 빈칸 앞에 긴 동격구와 관계절을 두어 주절의 끝이 흐려지게 했다. 학생은 'Émile had borrowed'가 이미 완전한 독립절이라는 점과, 'by the time' 부사절 뒤에도 주절이 따로 이어진다는 점을 둘 다 확인해야 한다.
g.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Émile had borrowed the net ... on the porch'는 긴 동격구가 붙어 있지만 완전한 독립절이고, 빈칸 뒤 'by the time the tide turned, the net had slipped ...'도 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 정답은 C이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 오용(comma splice)이 된다. B는 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D는 'where'가 'porch'를 수식하는 관계절을 시작하지만, 그 관계절 안에 이미 'the net had slipped'라는 완전한 절이 들어 있어 구조가 맞지 않고 의미도 엉뚱해진다(그물은 현관에서 미끄러진 것이 아니다).
g.explanation_en: The words before the blank, "Émile had borrowed the net ... on the porch," form a complete independent clause, even with the long appositive attached. The words after the blank, "by the time the tide turned, the net had slipped ...," form a second independent clause with its own subject and verb. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, so C is correct. A joins them with only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on. D turns "where" into a relative clause modifying "porch," but the clause that follows is already complete, so the structure doesn't work, and the meaning is wrong too: the net didn't slip from the porch.
